newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT second quarter net more than doubles.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT second quarter net more than doubles.

text.p: Dutch paper and office equipment group NV Koninklijke KNP BT reported a second quarter total net profit of 105 million guilders ($50.8 million) on Thursday, more than double the 51 million posted in the year-ago period.
The company's second quarter net profit from ordinary operations rose to 85 million guilders from 51 million, at the higher end of analysts's expectations.

KNP BT repeated it expected the 1997 full-year profit to show a substantial increase, but warned that results at its paper production division KNP Leykam would remain under pressure despite healthy volume growth.
Chief financial officer Rob Bonnier told a news conference that KNP BT's business had picked up in the second quarter of 1997 after a slow start.
"The year has begun a bit sluggishly, but later we have found some momentum," Bonnier said.
He said KNP BT's Distribution division had very good prospects given its order position and at KNP Packaging margins were seen rising later this year due to price hikes.
Despite the profit rise, analysts were not impressed by KNP BT's figures.
"Underlying, this is not the improvement we had hoped for. Distribution and packaging are not the activities which will show a huge profit jump,' said Pieter van Gelder at Delta Lloyd Bank.
Analyst Johan van den Hooven at NIB Securities said the results were at the top end of consensus, but pointed out that they included a 20 million guilder extraordinary gain.

On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, KNP BT's share price fell after the results were published. The shares closed at 47.60 guilders, down 1.10 from Wednesday's closing level and below a 51.20 guilder session high reached earlier on Thursday. ($ = 2.066 Dutch Guilders)
